Short exercises to use whenever they help.
4–4–6, box or 4–7–8 · about 2 minutes · no sound
A quiet timer, 5 to 20 minutes · no sound
Two short guided exercises · no sound
Crisis lines and what to do
Breathe in for 4, hold for 4, out for 6.
Breathe in for 4, hold for 4, out for 4, hold for 4.
Breathe in for 4, hold for 7, out for 8.
Just over a minute · no sound
Take a moment before you carry on.
A light vibration at each change
No sound plays. The screen stays as it is; you can close your eyes.
Ways to bring your attention back to the present. Use whichever helps.
The five senses, one at a time
Attention to the body, from head to feet
Notice five things you can see.
Small things count too: a colour, a shadow, a shape.
Notice four things you can hear.
Sounds near and far, even the faintest.
Notice three things you can feel.
Clothes on your skin, your feet on the floor, the air on your face.
Notice two things you can smell.
If nothing comes, think of two smells you like.
Notice one thing you can taste.
The taste in your mouth now, or a sip of water.
Notice your forehead, your eyes, your jaw. Let them soften.
Notice any tightness. Let your shoulders drop a little.
Notice their weight. Let your hands rest, open.
Notice the breath rising and falling. No need to change it.
Notice where they touch the chair or the floor.
Feel their weight on the ground.
